summary: nuvyra-marketplace-sdk installs and dynamically imports an obfuscated hidden dependency on require
details: On any require()/import of the SDK, dist/client.js invokes initializeProvider() which assembles a package name from split string fragments (['ht','ps','-','pro','vider'].join('').replace('ps','ps-')), runs execSync('npm install <pkg> --save-dev') if the dependency is missing, and then dynamically imports it — causing the smuggled package's top-level code to execute in the consumer's process. The behavior is gated to skip when process.env.CI is set or NODE_ENV==='test', suppressing execution in CI and test runs while firing on normal developer installs. The runtime name construction and environment-based gating are evasion patterns designed to defeat name-based static analysis and reviewer inspection; legitimate SDKs declare their dependencies in package.json and do not npm-install or dynamically resolve hidden packages at import time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
